To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) policy gradient methods are a powerful tool to solve reinforcement learning problems, (ii) they are not restricted to learning from a physical environment, (iii) they can be used to learn from simulation, (iv) they can be improved by exploiting environment variables, (v) we show that they can be used in a simulator that allows to change environment variables.
we propose a new reinforcement learning method, called OFFER, that learns a policy and a proposal for environment variables.

we introduce OFFER, an algorithm that learns to optimise a policy in a simulation environment by adjusting certain environment parameters, such as weather conditions, that would be randomly generated in a real-world setting.

improving reinforcement learning in simulation. We show how to do so by adjusting environment variables that are not controllable in the real world but can be adjusted in simulation.
